themes_detail.label: E-Scooter Surge
themes_detail.summary: E-scooter complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.6 per week (331% increase, z-score 6.27), signaling rapid expansion of micromobility operations or user violations in Jamaica/Hollis/St. Albans that may pose safety and infrastructure hazards.
evidence: 7 e-scooter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
331% spike with z-score of 6.27 (statistically significant at high severity)
No prior mention in community board agendas or local news, suggesting new or under-reported phenomenon
reporting_angles: Which scooter companies are operating in the district and what are residents complaining about (blocking sidewalks, reckless riding, lack of parking)?
Are there hot spots (schools, transit hubs, commercial corridors) where e-scooter violations cluster?

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 33 LAST WEEK versus 12.2 weekly average (169% increase, z-score 5.46), potentially indicating coordinated renovation activity, infrastructure work, or contractor violations affecting residents.
evidence: 33 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 12.2 weekly baseline (169% increase)
Z-score of 5.46 indicates high statistical significance
795 DOB building permits filed in 90 days (512 alterations), suggesting active construction environment; spike may reflect inadequate contractor oversight or permit compliance
reporting_angles: Are DOB permits concentrated in specific neighborhoods within CD412 or linked to major development projects (Atlantic Avenue, Station Plaza)?
What are residents complaining about—noise, debris, lack of permits, water shutoffs, or hazardous conditions?

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Complaints Resurge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints surged to 6 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.8 per week (700% increase, z-score 6.33), indicating either a new concentration of street drinking, lax enforcement, or environmental changes creating conditions for public alcohol consumption.
evidence: 6 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike)
Baseline was near-zero, suggesting this is either a new emergence or a sudden policy/enforcement shift
reporting_angles: Are there specific streets, parks, or transit corridors where public drinking is concentrated?
Has NYPD enforcement changed, or has a new venue/condition (homeless encampment, closed shelter, new bar) contributed to the spike?

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK from 0.9 weekly average (471% increase, z-score 5.28), likely reflecting unlicensed dispensaries, improper operations, or neighborhood opposition to legal retail expansion in Jamaica/Hollis.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (471% increase)
Spike suggests rapid proliferation of retail operations, either licensed or unlicensed
reporting_angles: How many legal cannabis dispensaries have opened in CD412 in the past 2-4 weeks, and where?
Are residents complaining about unlicensed shops, odor, loitering, or proximity to schools/parks?

themes_detail.label: Root, Sewer & Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about root, sewer, and sidewalk conditions nearly doubled to 16 LAST WEEK from 7.0 weekly average (129% increase, z-score 4.5), mirroring repeated community board budget requests for sidewalk repair—suggesting chronic infrastructure neglect is accelerating.
evidence: 16 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints last week vs. 7.0 weekly average (129% increase, z-score 4.5)
Community board has submitted repeated annual budget requests for sidewalk/curb repair and DEP capital investment, indicating a long-standing but worsening issue
Converges with 'General Construction/Plumbing' spike, suggesting active infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Which blocks or neighborhoods have the worst sidewalk damage, and how long have residents been reporting them?
Does DEP have a repair backlog in CD412, and what is the timeline for addressing prioritized locations?
